source_refs.note: Limitations: a main subheading of 28.3 Thin-Layer Chromatography, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 179-181.

items: TLC is mainly a qualitative technique and can only give an idea about the amount of a substance. So, TLC is not accurate and precise quantitative technique.
TLC cannot clearly separate compounds having close Rf values. Hence resolution of spots is not always high and sharp.
In TLC, only small amounts of sample can be applied and analysed. It is not suitable for large-scale separation.
This technique is sensitive to humidity, temperature and cleanliness of working environment which reduces reproducibility.

blocks.prompt: a) A mixture contains butanone and pentane. How can they be separated by using thin layer chromatography using aluminium oxide as stationary phase and benzene as solvent?
blocks.explanation: Spot the mixture on the baseline and stand the plate in benzene. Butanone is polar (C=O group), so it is held more strongly by the polar aluminium oxide and moves less far (lower Rf). Pentane is non-polar, dissolves better in benzene and moves further (higher Rf). Two separate spots form, which can be seen with iodine vapour or UV light.

blocks.prompt: b) A mixture of two substances X and Y is analysed by thin-layer chromatography. The Rf value of substance X is larger than that of substance Y. Suggest why substance X has a larger Rf value.
blocks.explanation: X is more soluble in the mobile phase (solvent) and/or is held less strongly by the stationary phase than Y (for example, X is less polar), so it moves further with the solvent.

blocks.alt: A chromatogram of three hair dyes. Dye A gives one spot low on the plate, dye B one spot high on the plate, and dye C two spots, one at the height of A's spot and one at the height of B's.
blocks.caption: Quick Check 28.1(c): Chromatogram of the hair dyes A, B and C (original drawing after the chromatogram printed in Quick Check 28.1).

blocks.prompt: c) A separate thin layer chromatography experiment was done using the hair dyes A, B and C. The chromatogram obtained is shown. State three conclusions about the hair dyes A, B and C which can be deduced from the chromatogram.
blocks.explanation: A and B each give only one spot, so each contains a single dye. C gives two spots, so C is a mixture. The spots of C are at the same heights as the spots of A and B (same Rf values), so C contains both dyes A and B. (B has the higher Rf, so B is more soluble in the solvent than A.)
